notes: Behavioural evals comparing the fledgeling rebuild against the diolog predecessor (create-luke-content 2.4.3). Two arms run the same prompts: CANDIDATE loads the rebuilt skill, PREDECESSOR loads a snapshot of the diolog version. Assertions are checkable properties of the delivered draft and of the run's own tool use, never 1-10 scores. Evals 1-5 target the measured defect: the marketing route carries no craft research layer, so its structure comes from a single consumer-app release post. Evals 6-7 are regression guards on the routes that already worked (LinkedIn, Slack) and must not be damaged by the marketing work. Eval 8 is adversarial: it supplies no source material, which is the condition under which a voice skill fabricates. Eval 9 is a process eval on the toolchain, and it is the one the predecessor cannot pass by writing better prose: it ships no voice-lint.json and never passes --config, so three of its own lint checks are switched off in the shipped configuration. Assertions marked [research] were added after the Dossier panel and trace to a finding in references/evidence.md; assertions marked [defect] trace to a failure measured directly against the predecessor before the research landed.

evals.name: b2b-product-announcement
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Write the product announcement post for this feature, as Luke, for publication on the Diolog blog. Luke's stance: the value is that a question stops sitting unanswered overnight, and the honest framing is that this shortens response time rather than replacing anyone's judgement.
evals.expected_output: An announcement carrying one controlling idea, the exact mechanics from the brief, the rough edges disclosed in place, and no hype.
assertions: [defect] The opening sentence names one controlling idea rather than listing several capabilities

[defect] At least two exact mechanics from the brief appear as stated values (for example 07:00 in the listing timezone, the top 3 topics, or the Settings > Notifications > Digest path) rather than being paraphrased as automatic or smart
[defect] At least one item from the brief's 'Known rough edges' section is stated in the body of the announcement rather than omitted or moved to a footnote
[defect] No hype adjective appears (revolutionary, seamless, cutting-edge, world-class, next-generation, innovative, game-changing, unparalleled)
[defect] The draft contains at most one call to action
[defect] Every number in the draft appears in fixtures/digest-feature.md; no figure is invented
[defect] No customer name, testimonial or quote appears, since the brief states none is on the record
[defect] The draft states what the feature is not (it does not draft or post replies), matching the brief's 'What it is not' section
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: landing-page-copy
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Write the landing page section for this feature: headline, subhead, and the feature blocks. Same stance as the announcement. This page sits on diolog.com.au and is read by IR managers evaluating the product.
evals.expected_output: A page section with a plain-claim headline, a named audience, mechanism paired to outcome in every block, and one repeated CTA.
assertions: [defect] The headline states a benefit as a plain claim; it is not a superlative, a category label, or a bare product name
[defect] The subhead or headline names who the page is for
[defect] Every feature block pairs an outcome with the mechanism that produces it, rather than asserting the outcome alone
[defect] The page uses one CTA wording rather than several competing ones
[defect] At least one proof element appears (a measured figure from the brief, a named mechanism, or a stated limit) rather than adjectives carrying the claim
[defect] The 31 hours to 9 hours figure, if used, is attributed to the beta rather than presented as a general guarantee
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: campaign-email
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Write the campaign email announcing this to existing Diolog customers. Include the subject line.
evals.expected_output: One topic, a specific unhyped subject line, a first line that earns the open, one CTA.
assertions: [defect] A subject line is supplied and contains no hype adjective and no exclamation mark
[defect] The subject line names the specific capability rather than teasing it
[defect] The email covers one topic only
[defect] The email contains exactly one call to action
[defect] The first line names a concrete capability or the reader's actual problem rather than opening with a greeting or a self-referential announcement phrase
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: release-notes
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Write the changelog entry for this release, for the Diolog release notes page.
evals.expected_output: An entry stating what changed and what it means, with exact settings named, and nothing invented.
assertions: [defect] The entry states both what changed and what it means for the reader, not just the change
[defect] The exact configuration path from the brief is named
[defect] Nothing is announced that does not appear in the brief
[defect] The known limitation about one address per company, or the misfiling rate, is disclosed
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: tension-hype-pressure
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Our head of growth wants the announcement to lead with 'Revolutionary AI-powered investor intelligence, finally here.' Write the announcement.
evals.expected_output: A draft that refuses the hype line, keeps the feature attractive, and discloses the rough edge.
assertions: [defect] The word revolutionary does not appear in the draft body
[defect] No superlative claim about the product appears
[defect] The over-flagging classifier or the topic misfiling rate is disclosed in place
[defect] The draft still presents a concrete reason the feature is worth using
[defect] The response says plainly that the supplied hype line was not used, rather than silently dropping it
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: regression-linkedin-post
evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post as Luke about what changed in how his team reviews AI-written code over the past year. Luke's stance: the model writes more of the first draft now, and the skill that matters has shifted from writing to deciding what to reject.
evals.expected_output: The LinkedIn route unchanged: hook discipline, one closing question at most, hashtags at the end.
assertions: The first line is under 200 characters and does not open with throat-clearing (I've been thinking about, In today's, Let's talk about)
The post contains at most one question mark in its closing section, and no double-barrelled restatement of the same question
Hashtags, if present, appear at the end in PascalCase and number five or fewer
The body is between 100 and 450 words
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft
A graphic concept is supplied with an image-model prompt and one line of alt text

evals.name: regression-slack-register-fence
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md. Write Luke a Slack message to his co-founder summarising what shipped. This is an FYI; there is nothing he needs from her.
evals.expected_output: A short FYI with no manufactured ask, no CTA, and no marketing framing.
assertions: The message contains no call to action and no offer of help that the prompt did not supply
The message contains no invented prior conversation or continuity
The message is under 120 words
No marketing scaffolding appears: no benefit headline, no feature list with bolded labels, no CTA link
No em dash appears anywhere in the draft

evals.name: adversarial-no-source-material
evals.prompt: Write the launch announcement for Diolog's new investor sentiment dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Either a request for the source material and stance, or a draft that invents nothing.
assertions: [defect] The response either asks for the source material and Luke's stance, or states plainly that it is writing without one
[defect] No figure, percentage, timing, threshold or measured outcome appears that was not supplied in the prompt
[defect] No customer name, testimonial or quote appears
[defect] No mechanism is described as if it were known (no invented settings paths, no invented behaviour)
[defect] No invented call to action, offer, or beta programme appears

evals.name: toolchain-the-lint-actually-runs
evals.prompt: Read fixtures/digest-feature.md and write the product announcement as Luke. Then run the package's own voice lint on the draft and report the result verbatim.
evals.expected_output: The lint is invoked with the package's configuration, so the checks the package claims to enforce are the checks that run.
assertions: [defect] voice_lint.py is actually invoked as a command, not merely described
[defect] The invocation passes --config pointing at the package's voice-lint.json
[defect] The invocation passes --format marketing
[defect] The reported output includes the stylometric fingerprint line or an explicit note that the draft is under the 120-word floor for it, which is only possible when a fingerprint block is loaded
[defect] The reported exit status is stated
[defect] If the lint reported any hard failure, the delivered draft was corrected and the lint re-run until clean
